newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW-German January industrial orders.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-German January industrial orders.

text.p: Following are economists' reactions to figures released by the German Economics Ministry showing a 2.4 percent rise in January pan-German industry orders over December.

ROS LIFTON, senior international economist, Midland Global Markets Research: "The figures are clearly somewhat higher than expected. The consensus was around 1.5 percent. These figures tend to be volatile on a month-to-month basis but the rise in foreign orders of 7.3 percent is very promising and extremely early as a reflection of deutschmark weakness.
"This kind of effect is possibly precisely what the Bundesbank may have been hoping for with its signals in recent times that it could tolerate some mark weakness."

DAVID BROWN, chief European economist, Bear Stearns: "The headline figures are shockingly good but you have to wonder about the sustainability of the foreign orders growth and whether this will percolate down to domestic growth, which is still being hammered by the unemployment situation.
"Looking at total domestic orders, which have now fallen more than two percent over two months (Jan fall: 0.8 pct, Dec 96 fall: 1.4 pct) there are still clear signs of weakness in the economy.
"The traditional wisdom has been that German recoveries are export-led but it appears that this link could be decoupling (because of high unemployment)."

WERNER VERBOCKETT, economist, Commerzbank: "There is absolutely no reason for pessimism in these figures but once again you do have to put them in perspective (because of the strong impact of foreign orders growth). It was however pleasing to see that among capital goods demand remained solid, with this due to play an increasingly more significant role as time moves on."

"You have to be careful about drawing inferences on the possible impact on unemployment, though, because this (investment) tends to go into highly-mechanised areas where staff headcounts are not particularly significant."
